distractors.reason: We don't say 'listen quickly'. 'Quickly' describes speed of an action, not the quality of listening.
We don't say 'listen slowly'. 'Slowly' describes the speed of moving or doing, not attention.
We don't say 'listen fast'. 'Fast' is used with movement or speed, such as 'run fast', not with listening.

l1_interference: W języku polskim przysłówek zwykle stoi przed czasownikiem ('uważnie słuchać'), dlatego osoby mówiące po polsku często mówią 'carefully listen' zamiast poprawnego 'listen carefully'.
explanation: In English, the adverb usually comes after the verb in this pattern. 'Carefully' tells us how someone listens, so the verb comes first and the adverb follows.

related_collocations.example: She can speak English fluently after three years of study.
My brother works hard every day.
Try to drink tea in the evening so you can sleep well.

memory_tip: VERB first, ADVERB second: listen carefully, work hard, sleep well (the adverb describes HOW the action happens)
